_comment: Per-voice (espeak-ng voice code, e.g. 'en-us') whitelist of multi-codepoint IPA
phoneme atoms that must NOT be split by tokenize_phoneme_word()'s longest-match
algorithm -- diphthongs, affricates, and any other multi-character unit that is
NOT expressible as 'base char + combining mark' (length marks, nasalization, etc.
are already handled generically by is_attaching() and never need to be listed here).
To add a new language: add a new '<voice-code>': [...] entry below. Do NOT edit
preprocess_ipa_childes_split.py -- the longest-match algorithm is language-agnostic,
only this data file is language-specific. Voice codes are matched exactly first
(normalized to lowercase with '_' -> '-'), then fall back to the part before the
first '-' (e.g. an unlisted 'en-gb' falls back to 'en'). If a voice has no match at
all, tokenize_phoneme_word() still works correctly for it -- it just won't merge any
language-specific multi-character atoms beyond the generic combining-mark rule.
These atoms decide which multi-codepoint units become single entries in the phoneme
vocab.txt, which is exactly what IPASymbolTokenizer's longest-match text_to_tokens()
uses to re-derive atomic tokens from the concatenated word strings at train time.
